headline: JSW Steel Limited: Disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations (Regulation 31(4))
sum: JSW Steel has filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure with NSE under the SEBI Takeover Regulations, signalling a substantial acquisition of shares event or related takeover milestone.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosures typically mark a critical gating point in M&A lifecycle—either the triggering of open offer thresholds (25% for listed companies under Reg 3) or post-open-offer regulatory mechanics; confirms SEBI Takeover Code is operative and acquirer identity and shareholding detail is now formally on record with the exchange.
detail: JSW Steel Limited has submitted a formal disclosure under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 to the National Stock Exchange (NSE). Regulation 31(4) typically mandates disclosure of material acquisition events, post-open-offer shareholding or acquirer identity confirmations. The filing on 24 June 2026 indicates a significant corporate action event requiring regulatory transparency under the takeover code. Specific parties, share count, offer price and conditions remain to be corroborated from the underlying disclosure document itself.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 3
framework.note: Defines substantial acquisition trigger at 25% of voting capital; central threshold for all takeover code compliance
Mandatory disclosure requirement for acquirers post-acquisition or post-open-offer closure; central to this filing
If acquisition breaches 25% threshold, open offer to public shareholders becomes mandatory
Board composition and director qualification rules; may apply if acquirer gains board seats post-acquisition
If acquirer is foreign entity, FDI approval under Press Note 3 or sectoral caps may apply; metals & mining sector subject to review

framework.ref: Ministry of Steel Regulations / Foreign Investment in Steel Sector
framework.note: Steel sector subject to specific foreign investment policy guidelines; applicable if acquirer is non-Indian

framework.ref: SEBI Regulations on Delisting (2012, as amended)
framework.note: If open offer leads to delisting, de-listing threshold (90% post-offer) and tendering mechanics apply

framework.ref: Listing Agreement / SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015, Regulation 30
framework.note: Continuous disclosure obligation for material corporate actions; JSW Steel must disclose key terms on exchange

conditions: Regulation 31(4) disclosure filed with NSE; indicates a substantial acquisition event has occurred or is imminent
Likely conditional on receipt of SEBI no-objection / regulatory clearance if foreign acquirer
Possible condition: public shareholders tendering threshold for open offer (if applicable)
approvals: NSE filing and acknowledgment (completed as of 24 Jun 2026)
Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) or Ministry of Steel approval (if foreign acquirer)
Board of Directors approval by acquirer and target
structure.novel: Regulation 31(4) creates a dual-disclosure regime: acquirer must disclose to target, and both must file with exchange. This particular filing appears to mark formal regulatory notification of a substantial acquisition milestone.

triggers.note: Mandatory disclosure of substantial acquisition details within 4 working days of open offer closure or acquisition completion
Regulator has authority to enforce disclosure and oversee orderly conduct of takeover
If acquirer is foreign entity, FDI route and sectoral caps trigger automatic RBI/Govt reporting
